title: White musicians jamming uptown after hours
summary: Benny Goodman, Harry James and others come up to jam and borrow riffs.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: there was Mexico's, Pod's and Jerry's, private houses in the basement there, they used to have a piano. Now, you could go in there and buy a drink, because it didn't cost nothing then, and sit down, and you could play if you wanted. Piano players would come in -- those white fellows -- Benny Goodman, he was up every morning. So was Harry James, so was the fellow -- I could go on, name after name. They used to come up and jam, and jamming there, they would listen, stuff like that.

Even one time had Louis up there. He was jamming Saturday nights at Lafayette Hall. That was a big hall on the 31st Street side. And all of them used to come up, because naturally, they have a pencil, they'd take down a riff if they liked something. A little later came a new record and you'd hear that same riff.
